Here are five tips to build your first one: Pick one task you do repeatedly (tagging, routing, weekly recaps) Write clear instructions: the goal, the format, and what to do when it's unsure Add a trigger (on a schedule or when X happens) so it runs in the background Start with the minimum permissions it needs. You can expand later. Test run → tweak → test again.

Women deserve to know their options for treating vaginal dryness and painful sex. On unPAUSED, we discuss low-dose vaginal estrogen and its role in treating genitourinary syndrome of menopause, or GSM. If lubricants are the only option you’ve been offered, ask whether vaginal estrogen could be appropriate for you. For my mother. For my grandmother. For my daughters. 🤍 As I grieve the loss of my mother, I’m holding close the love that connects the generations of women in my family. I cannot control everything about how I age. But I can take steps today to protect my strength, support my brain health, and lower my risk of frailty and dementia. That is part of my “why.” Why I lift weights. Why I move my body. Why I pay attention to nutrition, sleep, and the supplements I choose based on my individual needs. There are no guarantees. I’ve been a physician for decades, and this one surprised me. Dense breasts don’t just make cancer harder to spot on a mammogram. They also raise your risk of breast cancer. About half of women have dense breasts, and many don’t know what that means for their screening. This week on unPAUSED, breast oncologist, Eleonora Teplinsky, MD breaks down when to ask your doctor about an MRI or ultrasound. ✨Listen to the full episode at the link in bio.  #breastcancer #breastcancerawareness #breastcancersupport  #womenshealth #healthcare

The menopause guideline most OB-GYNs have practiced under was written in 2014, before the newest nonhormonal drugs existed and before the FDA changed the hormone therapy label. On October 15, ACOG replaced it: Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology (2026), covering hot flushes, sleep, and mood. Hormone therapy is strongly recommended for hot flushes and the sleep disruption they cause, started before 60 or within 10 years of menopause; continuing past 60 may be necessary if symptoms persist.
